ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Anna and Peter live in the same street. On one side of Anna's house there are 27 houses, and on the other side 13 houses. Peter lives in the house right in the middle of the street. How many houses are there between Anna's and Peter's houses?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows Anna's shaded house on a street. The label 27 is shown on one side of Anna's house, and the label 13 is shown on the other side, indicating there are 27 houses on one side of Anna and 13 houses on the other side. Reasoning: Include Anna's own house to get the total number of houses on the street: 27 + 1 + 13 = 41. Since Peter lives in the house exactly in the middle of the street, Peter is in the 21st house from either end, because the middle of 41 houses is position (41 + 1) / 2 = 21. Numbering from the side where there are 27 houses before Anna, Anna is the 28th house. The position gap between Anna and Peter is 28 - 21 = 7. The number of houses between them is one less than the gap, so 7 - 1 = 6.
